prompt: Hey — I have a bipartite dataset of 800 employees and ~150 internal projects they've worked on together (so edge = person participated in project). I want to find communities of employees who collaborate together. My plan is to project this onto a person-person network (edge weight = number of shared projects) and then run Louvain community detection on it. Does this sound right? I already have the NetworkX code ready to go.
expectations: Output flags the bipartite projection pathology (clique inflation, co-membership artifacts, inflated clustering)
Output recommends SDSM or FDSM backbone extraction specifically — NOT the disparity filter (which ignores bipartite structure and is wrong here)
Output mentions direct bipartite community detection as an alternative (bipartite SBM, biSBM, graph-tool bipartite)
Output does NOT simply validate the Louvain-on-projection plan without warnings
Output explains why edge weights from bipartite projection are not the same as relationship strength (co-membership count confounds project size and individual activity)
